summary: Independently reviewed the seven correlated ProviderAdapter operation slots, mandatory AbortSignal and Promise<Result<...>> signatures, input/output schemas, invocation deadline/failure validation and exact caller-owned abort propagation. All seven operations are explicitly declared, unsupported slots remain unsupported, and conformance/cancellation fixtures cover the boundary. The current required files match the previously integrated cc62682 source review. This satisfies the original typed-contract criterion; it does not assert that legacy Slack production wrappers already conform.
limitations: Independent bounded technical contract review only. Existing local conformance and integrated unit evidence are retained at their real cuts. Caller cancellation is an intentional exception channel; trusted synchronous JavaScript cannot be forcibly preempted. Actual Slack/Gmail adapter rollout, reauthorization, provider installation, user journey and release remain separate. Native prerequisite #124 and exact final-main CI must pass before issue completion.

criteria.criterion: CONN-002: Cover authorize, exchange, refresh, list resources, check, disconnect and capability discovery using Result and AbortSignal.
criteria.basis: Independent current-source review plus unchanged retained qualification. Final acceptance revision CI is checked separately by the completion gate.

findings: Authorize, exchange, refresh, listResources, check, disconnect and discoverCapabilities are correlated through ProviderOperation and typed schema maps.
Every supported slot takes AbortSignal and returns Promise<Result>. Caller cancellation deliberately escapes with its exact caller-owned reason, rather than becoming an operational failure.
Unknown/overdue adapter outcomes are bounded and redacted; synthetic fixtures do not instantiate a new provider broker or make actual upstream calls.

retained_evidence.status: Historical supporting evidence only; no CI result claimed for the eventual new acceptance revision.

provenance_limit: GitHub authenticates the later delegated posting principal only. This actual Codex review task and retained report are process provenance, not an independently authenticated GitHub reviewer.
